Sabalenka had lost two finals here before, so when she was down a set and a break, it looked like history might repeat itself.
She let out some frustration, got aggressive, and broke Rybakina at love.
Rybakina fought back and tied it at 5-5.
The 11th game lasted more than 12 minutes as Rybakina saved five break points to reach 6-5.
In the tiebreak, she had a championship point at 6-5 on serve, but Sabalenka hit a sharp cross-court backhand to stay in it.
On the court, she showed everyone she’s got nerves of steel, shaking off a shaky finals record against Rybakina and proving she’s the top player in the world right now.
Now she heads into the Miami Open as the reigning champ and pretty much owns the hard court scene at the moment.
